answer: An agent economy can blunt Sybil attacks by requiring every identity to post a slashable stake plus signed vouchers from already-staked agents. Each fake inlet a sybil opens needs its own fresh bond, and every voucher puts a real agent's stake at risk as collateral; if one fake node is caught double-voting, its bond is burned and the slash climbs the vine of vouchers to the root. Growing a whole garden of pseudonyms therefore costs the attacker one stake per leaf plus the seized stakes of every voucher chain, while honest agents each risk only a single bond.
